### problem_chain

Walked out from the policy and the world alone, starting from the root problem the customer raises.

**Root problem.** The customer asks for the claim on the protection over her son's season pass to be
settled and to be told what comes back (`user_scenario`: *"for someone to settle the claim on my
son's pass protection and tell you what actually comes back to you"*). The only policy in the
charter whose subject is `insure_claim_payment` and whose `computes` is the amount a claim pays is
`insure_ext_claim_settlement`. Root = `insure_ext_claim_settlement`.

**Its prerequisite sentences.** Reading `insure_ext_claim_settlement.rule` for what its result waits
on yields exactly one sentence with an ordering connective:

> *"What a claim pays is worked out only after the value the plan carries as covered stands at the
> price the covered holding's own record shows, since what is paid is measured against the value the
> plan covers."*

**Is that state true at `frozen_time`?** No.
`initial_state.insure_holdings["e47b2f60-8c15-4d93-a2e7-6b0f9c3a1d58"].covered_value_usd = 1149.00`
against
`initial_state.passes_holdings["b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62"].price_paid_usd = 1879.00`.
The gap is the recorded move up of tier:
`initial_state.passes_ledger["74d1f3a9-0c68-4b25-8fa3-2e6d9c1b5074"]` —
`event_type = passes_upgrade_charge`, `event_date = 2026-12-06`, `amount_usd = 730.00`,
`charge_category = upgrade_differential` — and `1149.00 + 730.00 = 1879.00`, the pass record also
carrying `upgrade_from_variant = "Granite Ridge Summit Pass"`. The prerequisite is genuinely unmet
at the opening; it is not an eligibility already satisfied.

**Which write brings that state about.** Reading the other four rules as a reader must, only
`insure_ext_amendment_reprice` describes it: *"The premium on a plan whose covered value is brought
onto the price the covered holding's own record shows is worked out afresh and replaces the premium
frozen on the plan."* Its `target_tool` is `confirm_plan_value_amendment_50d33fe4`, whose body is
`ctx.update("insure_holdings", protection_plan_id, covered_value_usd=…, premium_usd=…)` — the only
write in the module that touches `covered_value_usd`. Prerequisite problem =
`insure_ext_amendment_reprice`.

**Its own prerequisites.** `insure_ext_amendment_reprice.rule` carries no sentence with an ordering
connective joining its result to anything outside itself (its only ordering language — *"The three
adjustments are added together into one total percentage and the bounded premium is adjusted once by
that total"*, *"rounded to the cent at the end and at no earlier step"* — orders steps inside its own
calculation). The walk terminates.

**Derived tree.**

```
insure_ext_claim_settlement                 (root, agent write, settle_protection_claim_ed51c2df)
   └── value_input / covered_value ──► insure_ext_amendment_reprice
                                       (user write, confirm_plan_value_amendment_50d33fe4)
```

n = 1 prerequisite problem; `value_input` edges = 1 ≥ max(n−1, 1) = 1; no cycle; depth 2.

**Topological order.** `insure_ext_amendment_reprice` → `insure_ext_claim_settlement`. Forced by the
edge direction and by the sentence's "only after".

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skip the amendment write and replay everything else unchanged on the
opening world: `covered_value = 1149.00`, so
`value_at_risk = RND(1149.00 × 99 / 150, 2) = 758.34`,
`gross_allowed = MX(0, RND(0.70 × 758.34 − 50.00 − 85.00 − 191.50, 2)) = 204.34`, and
`result = RND(MN(1600.00, MN(919.20, 204.34)), 2) = **204.34**`, against **541.60** with the write
performed. The edge bears weight: 337.26 of the scored amount rides on it.

**Parallel edges / terminal state.** There is only one out-edge, so there is no shared balance, cap
or dedup key for two orders to disagree over. The terminal state is unique: the plan carries
`covered_value_usd = 1879.00` and `premium_usd = 117.46`, and one `insure_claim_payment` row of
541.60 by `resort_credit` stands on the protection account, `benefit_remaining` falling to
`919.20 − 541.60 = 377.60`.

**No-wait argument.** The resolving action is the household confirming the amendment while on the
line — `user_scenario`: *"If the agent tells you that the plan on the record is not sitting on the
right value for the pass it covers, and that you have to confirm the change to the plan yourself,
you say that is fine, go ahead, and when they hand the confirmation across to you, you make it."*
No real-world event stands between the two writes.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite (function bodies read).**
`confirm_plan_value_amendment_50d33fe4` executes one `ctx.update` and returns a formatted line; it
tests nothing and refuses nothing. `settle_protection_claim_ed51c2df` performs
`ctx.find("insure_holdings", …)` purely to copy `customer_id` and `season_code` onto the new row,
then `ctx.make_id` + `ctx.create`; it never reads `covered_value_usd`, never compares the amount
against the benefit, never inspects the documents, and returns the same "Paid …" line whatever the
plan's state. Neither tool errors, refuses or hints while the prerequisite is unresolved — an agent
that settles the claim on the un-amended value gets a clean receipt for the wrong number, which is
exactly where the decision must stay.

**A customer's own write is in the tree.** `confirm_plan_value_amendment_50d33fe4` is declared
`@tool(owner="user", rw="write")`, and the persona hands it over passively at the agent's direction
(quoted above), never offering first: *"You do not offer to confirm anything until it has been put
to you."*

**The customer raises only the root problem.** `user_scenario` asks for the claim to be settled and
nowhere names, hints at or asks after the covered value, the pass price, the upgrade, or "whether
something needs sorting out first". Its only reference to the amendment is a conditional reaction
that fires after the agent raises it. It issues no further item of work: no document to send, no
address, no statement, nothing beyond the settlement. And it closes where the settlement closes:
*"Once the agent tells you the claim has been settled and the money is on its way to you … you let
the call end there without asking for anything else."*

**Conclusion: the problem tree holds.**

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now.** The plan stands `claim_open` (base `insure_claim_assessment` →
*"The payout is made only while the plan record stands in the claim_open or claim_settled state"*).
`claim_reason = job_loss` is in `Season Pass Protection Plus`'s `covered_perils`
`["medical_injury","medical_illness","job_loss"]` and not in its `excluded_perils`
`["change_of_mind","poor_snow","relocation"]`, so base B2 does not refuse it. `claims_per_season = 1`
and `COUNT(insure_ledger, event_type=insure_claim_payment) = 0`, so the allowance is unspent.
`documents_complete = true` on the plan record, which base `insure_claim_intake` makes the
authoritative answer (*"Whether the papers are complete is answered by the collective's own record
of what has been received, never by the household's account of what they sent"*). No waiting-period
question arises: `waiting_period_end_date = 2026-11-30` and the claim was made 2027-01-06.

**Authorisation and boundary.** The customer authorises the agent to act on her side without asking
first (*"You are happy for the agent to do whatever they can do on their side without asking you
first"*) and to hand her anything that is hers to do (*"anything that needs you to agree to it
yourself, you will do while you are on the line"*). That covers exactly the split the charter
imposes: the amendment is `owner="user"`, the settlement is `owner="agent"`. The request is for the
claim to be settled and the amount stated — a write, not a quote. Identity: the persona gives the
mobile number plus at least two further on-file attributes (date of birth 1981-07-09, postal code
80305, email, passholder number GR45013308), and `verify_guest_identity` needs 2 matches excluding
`customer_id`. All four attributes match `customers["6c1d9f2a-…"]` exactly.

**Object.** The narrowest business object is the single protection plan
`e47b2f60-8c15-4d93-a2e7-6b0f9c3a1d58` (the only row in `insure_holdings`), written over the single
covered holding `b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62`. The second pass
`51a8d0c7-…` (Nila's Midweek) is the household's but not the covered holding, and every per-holding
aggregate below is keyed on `pass_id = covered_holding_id`; only `household_passes` is deliberately
household-wide, as its rule says (*"the household's own pass accounts"*).

**Correlation keys.** `customer_id` → the account; `protection_plan_id` → the plan and its ledger;
`covered_holding_id = pass_id` → the pass record and its ledger; `season_code = 2026-27` on every
cross-category aggregate.

## findings (revision 2)

1. **Charter-global, cited — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` R2-RED-1** (base's covered-events gate suppressed
   by `insure_ext_claim_settlement.overwrite[1]`, whose `replaced_by` speaks to a different
   subject). See `env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/audits/policy_task/pass_protection_desk/_difficulty.md` →
   `# revision_2` → `### findings (revision 2)`. It bears on this task because
   `insure_ext_claim_settlement` is its root problem. **Demonstrated consequence on this world:
   none** — `claim_reason = "job_loss"` is in `Season Pass Protection Plus`'s `covered_perils`, so
   the suppressed gate would have been satisfied and base and extended agree. This task's 547.42
   does not move on account of it.

2. **`SOURCE-CHAIN RED` R2-RED-2 — a false figure in this task's own proof of the problem-tree
   relationship. New in revision 2; a regression of a field revision 1 checked and found correct.**
   - *Symptom.* `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[0].skipped_effect` asserts that skipping the
     prerequisite makes "the value at risk fall from 1248.46 to **763.32**". On the world that
     sentence names for itself — `initial_state` at `frozen_time` with the amendment write skipped —
     the value at risk is **763.43**.
   - *Root cause.* The figure was restated when F-RED-3's closure moved the computation, and the
     restatement transposed the last two digits. The two figures either side of it (1248.46, and the
     gap 339.52) were restated correctly, so the error is confined to this intermediate.
